summary:
Taraba stands under Nigeria's national criminal framework, which the parent record carries. No Taraba state statute, prosecution or enforcement incident was identified in the sources reviewed for this jurisdiction.

The one Taraba-specific legal fact documented is a negative one. The national legal overview lists the harsher Sharia-law penalties for same-sex conduct, lashing or caning up to death under state Zina provisions, only for the Nigerian states that have adopted Sharia penal codes, and Taraba is not among them. No death-penalty or corporal-punishment exposure under state Zina provisions is documented as applying in Taraba, so a trans visitor's exposure in this state rests on the federal statute rather than on a state Sharia code.
tangentialFactors:
Taraba's position differs from that of the northern Nigerian states that have adopted Sharia penal codes. A visitor crossing from Taraba into one of those states moves into a regime whose Zina provisions carry lashing or caning up to death for same-sex conduct, while Taraba's own exposure remains the federal one.

The sources reviewed record no Taraba-specific curfew, mobile-network shutdown or security operation.
localsOnly:
No Taraba-specific resident-facing facts were identified in the sources reviewed. No state ordinance, local government by-law, police directive or state-level enforcement practice bearing on trans residents appears in the inventory, and the national framework governs residents of Taraba as it governs visitors.

The sources contain no Taraba data on healthcare access, HIV service provision, or police conduct toward trans residents.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources reviewed are national in scope and none names a Taraba case, institution or official. Whether Taraba's police and courts enforce the federal statute at a rate above or below the national pattern is not sourced; no Taraba arrest, charge or prosecution under the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 or the criminal code was identified.

Taraba's exclusion from the Sharia-adopting states is documented through a national legal overview rather than a Taraba state gazette or penal code text. The state's own statute book was not reviewed directly in the sources available.

No Taraba-specific data on police extortion, app-based entrapment, violence against trans people, or access to trans health services was identified.
